From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>

Subject: Recap: FinLytics discovery + model evals / quant trade-offs

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so everyone has the same context.

Summary of needs:
- Real-time model-based summarization and entity extraction over investor reports (~1–2s latency target; 50k requests/day expected).
- Strong fidelity on numeric extraction and conservative hallucination behavior (false positives are costly).
- EU data residency; SOC 2 compliance required for vendor.

Initial model/eval recommendations (high-level):
- Candidate: Llama-3-32B (quant): good baseline for extraction accuracy. Recommend AWQ-int8 profile for throughput tests.
- Lightweight option: Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP8) for lower cost paths when latency is tighter.
- Eval plan: run our benchmark suite on your sample prompts (we discussed prompt sets A/B/C) and compare AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 on both accuracy and regression risk.

Key trade-offs to watch (covered in call):
- AWQ (aggressive quant) offers best throughput but can introduce subtle quality regressions on numeric precision unless prompt/eval coverage includes those edge cases.
- GPTQ tends to be steadier on fidelity but costlier at scale than AWQ for large models.
- FP8 (where supported) is promising for 7B-class models: lower latency + fewer regressions vs 4-bit AWQ on similar model size.

Attachments shared: finlytics_poc_scope.pdf (POC scope + timeline). I also uploaded our baseline benchmark CSV to the shared Drive and a short note outlining the quant trade-off checks (attached as eval-results-20260720.csv and quant-tradeoff-notes.md).

Next steps / asks:
1) Elena: confirm sample prompt sets and a handful (10–20) representative documents for the POC evaluation.
2) Redwood: we’ll run the benchmark across AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 profiles and provide a short trade-off report + recommended config for the POC (expected 3–4 business days after we have samples).
3) Schedule a 30-min technical kickoff (can be next Wed) — I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

If helpful, we can include a short config that runs AWQ for bulk throughput with an automatic fallback to a higher-fidelity GPTQ profile for requests flagged as high-risk by a lightweight classifier (we discussed this pattern).

Thanks — talk soon.

— Sergio

Internal notes / quick technical plan for POC (tagging @Aditya for the benchmark runs):

Short answer to Elena's regression question: we quantify numeric/format fidelity with three checks:
- Exact-match extraction tests for numeric fields (currency, decimals) against a labeled ground truth.
- Unit/scale sanity checks (e.g., detecting if a value was interpreted in millions vs thousands).
- Semantic consistency tests (secondary paraphrase prompts to catch hallucinated attributions).

Planned runs (once we have Elena's samples):
1) Baseline: Llama-3-32B float16 (unpinned) — get reference accuracy and latency.
2) AWQ-int8 profile on Llama-3-32B — measure throughput, latency, and run the numeric fidelity suite. Flag any precision deltas >0.5% or changed rounding behavior.
3) GPTQ-quant on same model — compare against AWQ; expect slightly higher cost but fewer fidelity anomalies.
4) Mistral-Instruct-7B FP8 run — target for low-cost / low-latency path; check extraction accuracy vs 32B variants.

Recommended POC config:
- Phase A (3 days): run all profiles on the 15 reports + 30 prompts, capture token-level latency, token cost, and three fidelity metrics above.
- Phase B (2 days): run stress throughput tests (concurrency up to 200 RPS), and test fallback routing: AWQ by default, auto-fallback to GPTQ when the lightweight classifier (threshold: confidence <0.75) flags a request.

Expected numbers (rough estimates; to be validated):
- Llama-3-32B AWQ-int8: 2.5–3x throughput vs float16; median latency ~800–1100ms for typical prompts; watch numeric rounding gaps.
- Llama-3-32B GPTQ: 1.8–2.2x throughput vs float16; slightly better numeric fidelity.
- Mistral-7B FP8: lowest latency (~350–600ms), cost-efficient for bulk but may miss edge-case extraction nuances.

Deliverables: tradeoff spreadsheet (eval-results-20260720.csv), recommendation memo (quant-tradeoff-notes.md). Aditya — please run the CSV exports and baseline graphs and drop them in the Drive folder.

— Marissa
